To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the T7 expression vector was used to express the HSV-1 RR small subunit (HSV-1 R2) in E. coli and that the expressed R2 could be purified to homogeneity.
the HSV-1 gene for the RR small subunit was cloned and the gene product was purified and characterized.
the HSV-1 ribonucleoside diphosphate reductase small (R2) subunit can be produced in Escherichio coli as an enzymically active protein and that the R2 subunit is not a dimer in solution.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the purification and characterization of HSV-1 RR expressed in E. coli.
the development of a T7 expression system for the production of the HSV-1 R1 and R2 subunits of RR.
the expression and purification of a functional herpes simplex virus type-1 (HSV- 1) ribonucleotide-reductase small sub-unit (R2).
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the HSV-1 RR is a heterodimer of two non-identical subunits, each of which is required for enzymic activity.
HSV-1 R1 and R2 are the only two proteins required for RR activity.
the HSV-1 RR is composed of a dimer of two 30 kDa R2 subunits, and that each R2 contains one atom of iron per R subunit.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have expressed the HSV-1 R1 and R2 genes in E. coli, purified the proteins and shown that they form an active enzyme.
the HSV-1 R1 and R2 subunits were expressed in E. coli and purified to homogeneity.
the HSV-1 RR is a dimer composed of two R1 subunits and two R2 subunits, and that the R1 subunit contains the catalytic centre of the enzyme.
The main takeaway from our work is that
it is possible to express the HSV-1 RR small subunit in E. coli in a manner which yields an enzymically active holoenzyme when combined with the E.
the T7 expression vector system can provide a rich source of the R2 protein for the preparation of the holoenzyme.
we have shown that it is possible to express the HSV-1 ribonucleoside reductase small and large subunits in bacteria, purify them to homogeneity and reconstitute the holoenzyme.
